subject: Discovery follow-up: schedule demo and loop in security & procurement
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpath.com>
Date: 2026-03-25T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery follow-up: schedule demo and loop in security & procurement

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call: 

• Summary: FinPath is evaluating a low-latency embeddings + chat solution for transaction monitoring and assistant workflows. Key constraints: PII handling, VPC connection to your analytics cluster, and predictable latency for query workloads.
• Goal: Schedule a 60-minute demo / technical deep dive next week to show a short architecture overview, live demo, and an ops/security Q&A.

Proposed windows (PT):
 - Tue Mar 30, 2026 — 10:00–11:00 AM PT
 - Wed Mar 31, 2026 — 1:00–2:00 PM PT

Can you confirm which works best and who from your side should join (security, procurement, platform)? I’ve attached my quick discovery notes and our datasheet for context.

Attachments: discovery_notes.pdf, redwood_datasheet.pdf

Thanks — I’ll loop in our security and platform leads once you confirm attendees.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0183

Hi Marissa — great recap, thanks. Either time works but we prefer Tue Mar 30 at 10am PT. I’ve looped in Marcus (procurement) and Jamie Park from security (cc’d).

For the technical deep dive, Jamie will lead the security questions. Please include your security lead on the thread so we can exchange requirements in advance. From procurement side, Marcus will handle the PO/SOW discussion after the demo.

Thanks,
Alex

Calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?id=abcd1234
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/FP-12458

 1) 10 min — Brief intro & high-level architecture

Marcus / Jamie — if you can confirm the attendee list from your side and any pre-read you want (e.g., network/IP allowlist, SOC 2) I’ll make sure we have everything ready.

Thanks — I’ll join the call on Mar 30. To make the session productive for your security team, could you share the following ahead of the call?

• Latest SOC 2 report or summary (PII/data classification handling)
• Encryption requirements (at-rest / in-transit) and key management (KMS/HSM) expectations
• Expected data flows (ingest -> storage -> inference) and whether any data stays on-prem
• Network topology / IP allowlist needs for VPC peering

I’ve attached a short SOC 2 summary from our side to start the exchange: SOC2-summary.pdf

If you prefer, we can use the first 10 minutes for any clarifying questions before diving into the demo.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Lead, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
